key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over hours to days. LOCATION: LOWER urinary tract (bladder, urethra). DURATION: Develops over hours to days, may persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: BURNING urination, frequency, urgency. AGGRAVATING: URINATION, sexual activity. RELIEVING: ANTIBIOTICS, increased fluid intake. TIMING: Gradual onset, develops over hours to days. SEVERITY: 4-7/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: BURNING URINATION, frequency, urgency, may have hematuria, may have fever if upper tract involved. KEY POSITIVES: Burning urination, frequency, urgency, positive urinalysis. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

includes.patient_friendly: lower right side around your groin

red_flags: Fever with urinary symptoms - possible pyelonephritis, call 911
Signs of severe infection - fever, chills, rigors - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
